name: Home Assistant
description: Search and control Home Assistant entities from the launcher, activate scenes, and expose your smart home to Asyar's AI agents.
author: Erwins Enkel

preferences.name: baseUrl
preferences.title: Home Assistant URL
preferences.description: Base URL of your Home Assistant instance, no trailing /api.

preferences.name: token
preferences.title: Long-lived access token
preferences.description: Home Assistant → your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create token. Stored encrypted on this device and never synced.

preferences.name: searchDomains
preferences.title: Domains offered in global search
preferences.description: Comma-separated entity domains. Narrow this to keep the root search bar uncluttered.

preferences.name: minQueryLength
preferences.title: Minimum characters before searching
preferences.description: Below this, the extension contributes nothing to global search.

commands.name: Home Assistant Entities
commands.description: Browse, filter, and control every entity

commands.name: Home Assistant Scenes
commands.description: Activate a scene or run a script

commands.name: Refresh Home Assistant State
commands.description: Background refresh of the cached entity list

tools.name: List Home Assistant entities
tools.description: List smart-home entities and their current state, optionally filtered by domain or a name fragment. Call when the user asks what devices exist, which lights are on, or what the state of a room is.

domain.description: Optional entity domain to filter by, e.g. 'light', 'switch', 'sensor', 'climate'.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive fragment matched against the entity's friendly name or id, e.g. 'kitchen'.

tools.name: Get Home Assistant entity state
tools.description: Get the current state and attributes of one specific entity. Call when the user asks about a single device, sensor reading, or whether something is on.

entityId.description: Full entity id, e.g. 'light.kitchen_ceiling'. Use ha-list-entities first if you only know the friendly name.

tools.name: Call a Home Assistant service
tools.description: Control a device by calling a Home Assistant service, e.g. turn a light on or off, activate a scene, set a temperature. Confirm with the user before calling this for anything disruptive.

service.description: Service name within the domain, e.g. 'turn_on', 'turn_off', 'toggle', 'set_temperature'.

data.description: Optional extra service data, e.g. { "brightness_pct": 40 } or { "temperature": 21 }.
